$comment: Which screen reaches each API route, checked by web/scripts/check-screen-coverage.mjs.
The route list is derived by parsing every .ts under api/src with the TypeScript
compiler and is not edited here: a route this file does not mention fails the build,
and an entry naming no route fails it too. Adding an endpoint means adding a line
Exactly one of `screen`, `waived_to` or `no_screen_owed` per entry. A `screen` is a
repository-relative path to a file inside web/ and must exist; anything more a reader
needs goes in `note`. A directory, `.` and `../..` all satisfied mere existence.
A `waived_to` must name one of the `stages` declared below -- without that the naming
requirement is satisfied by any non-empty string. `no_screen_owed` is for a route no
person ever reaches. The latter two carry a reason, because nothing can check either.
The check prints the three counts on every run, so read them there rather than here:
a number written in this comment is one nobody updates. It said thirteen of thirty-five
with twenty-one waived, and was stale the moment the first reporting route landed.
What the counts describe is the interface debt Stage 3 and Stage 4 accumulated with
nothing recording it (ruling of 2026-09-06), written down rather than found at the pilot.

routes.note: Called from every authenticated screen rather than from one.

routes.reason: §8 asks for the chain when a profile is opened: the profile names the person's direct leader from it, and My Network shows the whole chain.
The branch the Network screen opens on: the signed-in person, their direct disciples by name, and the headcounts of the tree now (decision 0252).
Anybody else's branch, when the address names them — focusing a row, the breadcrumb, Up one level and a search result all land here (decision 0252).
DCC records behind for the current month on each row and on the focus person, under dcc.view_subtree (decision 0252).
Cell Leaders beneath and Cell meetings behind for the current month, under cell.view_subtree (decision 0252).

Everyone beneath a leader, flat and paged. The Network screen goes one generation at a time and never needs it, and the People screen already lists the searcher's own scope (decision 0244), so no use for a second flat list has been named.
routes.waived_to: after the pilot — flat subtree view

routes.reason: The DCC report's By leader table: each leader's own records filed and owed, the rows adding up to the report's coverage (decision 0254).
The Cell report's By leader table: each leader's own meetings recorded and scheduled, the rows adding up to the report's coverage (decision 0254).
Reassignment is the highest-risk authorization surface in the system (§5). Move to another leader on the person's profile opens this dialog, which performs it.
Admin-only (§7, people.correct_sex), and it forces a Network change. It belongs to the Admin surface §19 describes, which the pilot does not need.

The index every other Cell route depends on (decision 0226). Cell Leaders is the screen in that block which shows it, and Dashboard reads it with ?led_by=me for a leader's own Cells (§19). Neither exists yet. It is ACTIVE-only, so it does not by itself discharge §19's requirement that a closed Cell's meetings stay reachable while their month is open.
The month's DCC events (decision 0227), read by the reader's month to place their own checklist on each Sunday and to show a removed Sunday with its reason.
The attention list behind each event's coverage figure (decision 0228, §15), reached from Reports, DCC, By Sunday.
The Cell roster (§12). Cell Attendance reads it, and it is the roster view §12 keeps separate from the statistical report.
Adding a member is part of running a Cell during the pilot month (§10).
The other half of membership, and a move is one transaction (§10).
A schedule change decides which meetings a month derives, so a pilot month needs it reachable (§10, §13).
§19's recording queue, and the only surface that names a closed Cell's meetings (ruling of 2026-09-17).
Cell Meetings. §19 puts meetings awaiting a record above the numbers on every leader's dashboard.
Who there is to record (§13). Cell Meetings calls it before a submission.
Recording a meeting is the thing the pilot exists to test — whether leaders record every week.
The DCC checklist (§9). A leader marking it must see who is already marked.
DCC recording, the second half of the pilot's month cycle (§9).
One person's DCC classification and the Sundays behind it (decision 0247), shown in the DCC section of the person profile.
The Cell a person belongs to, with its leader, and the Cells they lead (decision 0248), shown on the person profile and on Edit.
Direct creation is Admin's during the initial-encoding phase (§2, §10). New Cell, from the Cells list, is how the pilot's Cells are set up.
Configuration rather than operation (§10). Nothing in one pilot month requires changing a category.
A closure is never reversed (decision 0133), so it is deliberately not put in front of a pilot leader.
The Admin queue §19 describes. It pairs with the approve and decline routes below.
The Admin queue's action (§10). A pending request changes nothing until it is decided.
The other outcome of the queue, and a decision is final (decision 0147).

The DCC figures a leader reads (§9, §12, §20). Dashboard is the screen in that block which shows them, and it does not exist yet; the route lands first so the dated authorization walk it needs is reviewed once rather than alongside eight screens. Network Summary would be the drill-down and is deliberately not named here — the roadmap defers it past the pilot, outside this block.

Cell classification, and the monthly-attendance buckets §12 puts at Cell scope only. Cell Attendance is the screen in that block which shows them, and it does not exist yet. The screen owes more than this route returns: §12 requires the coverage line beside the buckets, and coverage is its own slice — so this waiver is not discharged by a screen that renders the buckets alone.
